items.title: Three Takeaways: November 23
items.summary: EXPECTATION IS CHANGING: Coach Klanderman appreciates people trying to console him after back-to-back losses to top-10 teams that could end up in the CFP Playoffs, but "the expectation is changing," he said. "And the expectation going forward is we're going to have success in those moments. There are a lot of things that need to take place between now and when we can do that, but that's forthcoming. .

items.title: Baylor Football Weekly Presser: Nov. 23
TAKE THREE
items.summary: WACO, Texas – Not that he hadn't had plenty of chances, but Baylor cornerback LeVar Thornton had gone 18 games without an interception.   That dry spell finally ended in the Bears' 20-10 loss to 11th-ranked Texas Tech on Saturday, when Thornton picked off a Tommy Castellanos pass at the goal line and returned it 23 yards early in the third quarter.

items.summary:
Baylor entered Saturday looking to break an eight-game skid to ranked teams at home. After being tied with the No. 12 Texas Tech at halftime, the Bears' offense struggled in the second half as the Red Raiders picked up the 20-10 win.

items.summary:
The Bears walked back onto the field at halftime tied with the second-best team in the Big 12 and the No. 12 team in the nation. Texas Tech then scored 10 unanswered points, totaled 257 yards and sacked junior quarterback DJ Lagway three times.
